title: Typography & Spacing for Readability ✍️
description: Choose fonts, line heights, and spacing that make reading effortless for everyone.

slides.title: Typography Is Accessibility 📖
slides.content:
Text is the core of the web. Readable text = accessible text.

* **Font choice**: sans‑serif generally easier on screens; avoid decorative fonts for body.
* **Size**: base font size of at least 16px; larger for reading comfort.
* **Line height**: 1.5 for body text.
* **Line length**: 45–75 characters per line (about 60ch).

Crowded text strains the eyes and increases cognitive load.

quizData.question: What is the recommended minimum line height for body text to meet WCAG 1.4.12 Text Spacing?
quizData.explanation: WCAG requires that users can override spacing without loss; a base of 1.5 ensures room for adjustment.

slides.title: WCAG 1.4.12: Text Spacing 📏
slides.content:
Users must be able to override:

* Line height to at least 1.5 times the font size.
* Spacing following paragraphs to at least 2 times the font size.
* Letter spacing to at least 0.12 times the font size.
* Word spacing to at least 0.16 times the font size.

Your layout must not break when these are applied via browser settings or custom CSS.

quizData.question: Why must a site not break when text spacing is increased?

options.text: Because users with dyslexia or low vision may need extra spacing
It's just a best practice, not a requirement

quizData.explanation: WCAG 1.4.12 exists specifically because many users need custom spacing to read effectively.

slides.title: Text Alignment & Justification 🔤
slides.content:
* **Avoid justified text** – creates uneven word spacing and "rivers of white" which are hard for dyslexic users.
* Left‑align text (for LTR languages) – the ragged right edge helps eyes track.
* Centre‑aligned text is okay for short headings, not for body.

Simple rule: left‑align, unless you have a very good reason.

quizData.question: Why is justified text problematic for many readers?

options.text: It creates uneven spacing and can cause 'rivers of white'
It doesn't work in all browsers

quizData.explanation: The inconsistent gaps between words disrupt the reading flow, especially for people with dyslexia.

slides.title: Font Readability Tips ✨
slides.content:
* Use a **large enough default font** (16px or 1rem).
* Choose fonts with **distinct letter shapes** (e.g., good 'I', 'l', '1').
* Avoid all‑caps for long text – harder to read.
* Ensure sufficient contrast (already covered, but typography depends on it!).
* Use `em` or `rem` for font sizes so they scale with user preferences.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Dyslexia‑friendly fonts
Consider using fonts like OpenDyslexic or Comic Sans (yes, really) in user‑customisable themes. They can improve readability for some.
